verse.text: He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.
verse.summary: Isaiah spoke these words to a people worn down by exile, who had begun to whisper that God no longer saw their struggle or cared about their cause. His answer was to point them to the Creator who never faints and never grows weary — and then to promise that this same untiring strength is handed to people who have run out of their own. Notice who qualifies: not the strong, but the faint; not the capable, but those with no might at all. If you are coming into today empty, you are exactly the kind of person this promise was written for.

sermon.title: When the Thorn Stays
sermon.excerpt: Paul prayed three times for the thorn to leave, and it stayed. But heaven's answer wasn't silence — it was grace enough to carry it, and the power of Christ resting on the very place he felt weakest.

bibleStudy.title: Where Are Thine Accusers?

verses.text: And the scribes and Pharisees brought unto him a woman taken in adultery; and when they had set her in the midst, They say unto him, Master, this woman was taken in adultery, in the very act. Now Moses in the law commanded us, that such should be stoned: but what sayest thou? This they said, tempting him, that they might have to accuse him. But Jesus stooped down, and with his finger wrote on the ground, as though he heard them not. So when they continued asking him, he lifted up himself, and said unto them, He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her. And again he stooped down, and wrote on the ground. And they which heard it, being convicted by their own conscience, went out one by one, beginning at the eldest, even unto the last: and Jesus was left alone, and the woman standing in the midst. When Jesus had lifted up himself, and saw none but the woman, he said unto her, Woman, where are those thine accusers? hath no man condemned thee? She said, No man, Lord. And Jesus said unto her, Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more.

Therefore thou art inexcusable, O man, whosoever thou art that judgest: for wherein thou judgest another, thou condemnest thyself; for thou that judgest doest the same things. But we are sure that the judgment of God is according to truth against them which commit such things. And thinkest thou this, O man, that judgest them which do such things, and doest the same, that thou shalt escape the judgment of God?

There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus hath made me free from the law of sin and death.

bibleStudy.excerpt: They brought stones for a woman's sin, got convicted by their own conscience one by one, and the only man left standing with the right to throw one laid it down instead.
body: Picture the setup before you picture the sin, because the setup is the real crime scene. John 8 opens with scribes and Pharisees parading a woman into the temple court, "taken in adultery, in the very act," and setting her in the midst where the whole crowd that had gathered to hear Jesus teach could get a good look. They weren't actually interested in her. The text says it outright: "This they said, tempting him, that they might have to accuse him." She is not the target. She is the bait. Moses' law did carry a death sentence for adultery, so on paper they're holding the moral high ground and the legal high ground at the same time, and they know it. Here's my real question for you today: how many times have you watched somebody else's sin get weaponized by people who never once cared about the sinner, only about the argument she could win them?

Watch what Jesus does with a room full of people demanding an immediate verdict: nothing, on purpose. "Jesus stooped down, and with his finger wrote on the ground, as though he heard them not." He lets the silence sit there until it gets uncomfortable, because silence is its own kind of answer to a trap question. Everybody wants to know what He wrote — preachers have guessed everything from a list of the accusers' own sins to a single verse of the law — but the text doesn't tell you, because the content was never the point. The posture was the point: a stooped, unhurried, unpanicked response to a mob that expected Him to either condemn a woman on the spot or discredit the law of Moses on the spot. He refused both doors they built for Him. Sometimes the most powerful thing you can do when somebody hands you a trap question is simply not answer it on their timeline.

Then He stands up and gives them exactly the verdict format they asked for, except He attaches a qualifier that turns their own weapon back on them: "He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her." That is not Jesus abolishing the law. That is Jesus enforcing the part of the law they conveniently forgot to mention — a charge like this required witnesses who could stand in genuine innocence of what they were accusing, not just witnesses with good eyesight. Paul writes the commentary on exactly this move in Romans: "Therefore thou art inexcusable, O man, whosoever thou art that judgest: for wherein thou judgest another, thou condemnest thyself; for thou that judgest doest the same things." Every accuser standing in that courtyard had just volunteered, by picking up a stone, to be judged by the exact standard they were about to apply to somebody else. That is the most dangerous math a self-righteous person can do, and most of them never see it coming until the verdict lands on their own head.

"And they which heard it, being convicted by their own conscience, went out one by one, beginning at the eldest, even unto the last." I want you to sit with the order of departure, because it's funnier and more damning than most sermons let it be. The eldest leave first. Not the youngest, still green, still working out their theology. The eldest — the ones with seniority, the ones with the longest résumé in the religion business, the ones who had been keeping score on other people's sins the longest. Apparently a longer career gives you a longer list of your own. Conscience didn't need a sermon to do its job in that courtyard; it just needed one sentence and some quiet. One by one, oldest to youngest, every stone-carrying hand in that crowd found a reason to be somewhere else, and nobody had to drag a single one of them out.

"And Jesus was left alone, and the woman standing in the midst." Read that sentence slowly, because it's the whole gospel compressed into nine words: the only man in the building actually qualified to throw the stone is the only man left standing, and He's the one who doesn't pick it up. "When Jesus had lifted up himself, and saw none but the woman, he said unto her, Woman, where are those thine accusers? hath no man condemned thee?" And her answer is the shortest, most stunned line in the whole chapter: "No man, Lord." Every voice that had come to destroy her had already left the room. The only voice that stayed had every legal right to finish what they started, and chose not to.

"And Jesus said unto her, Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more." This is where people get the gospel half right and miss the better half. Jesus did not say the sin wasn't real — He named it in the very next clause, which only makes sense if there was something real to stop doing. Grace was never Jesus pretending the stone wasn't deserved. Grace was Jesus being the only person in that courtyard with the standing to throw it, and laying it down anyway. Paul writes the theology of that exact moment four chapters into Romans: "There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus... For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus hath made me free from the law of sin and death." Not no condemnation because the law got rewritten. No condemnation because the Judge became the one who absorbs the sentence instead of handing it down.

Here's my real question for you today, and I need you to actually answer it instead of skimming past it: in this story, which hand are you? Are you the one holding a stone, keeping a private list of somebody else's failures while conveniently forgetting the inventory of your own? Romans 2 already told you how that ends — you condemn yourself the moment you condemn someone for the thing you also do, just more quietly, in rooms nobody audits. Or are you the woman standing in the middle of the courtyard, certain the verdict is already written, flinching for a stone that never comes, because the only person with the right to throw it decided mercy was the better use of His authority?

Notice what the story doesn't give you: a woman who argues her innocence, a Jesus who pretends the sin away, or a crowd that gets a cheap redemption arc. It gives you dropped stones on temple flagstones, an empty courtyard where a lynching was supposed to happen, and one sentence that still has enough weight to hold up two thousand years later — go, and sin no more. Not stay as you were. Not feel better about what you were. Go, in a new direction, carrying a verdict of no condemnation instead of the stone you were braced for. That's not a loophole in the law. That's the law's whole debt getting paid by somebody else so you could walk out of the courtyard standing instead of buried under it.

So before you pick up the next stone for somebody else's sin, remember whose courtyard you're actually standing in. The accusers walked in with the law on their side and walked out convicted by their own conscience before Jesus ever opened His mouth against them. The woman walked in expecting to die and walked out with a sentence of mercy she never asked for and did not deserve by the letter of the law she broke. That is the gospel in one courtyard: the guilty walking free, and the self-righteous walking out quietly embarrassed, one by one, beginning at the eldest. Put the stone down. Go, and sin no more. In Jesus' name, amen.

lines: Father, I declare today that Your grace is sufficient for me — not barely enough, but more than enough!
I will not measure Your love by the thorn that stayed — You answered me, and Your answer is grace!
The weak place in my life is not my end — it is where Your strength is made perfect!
I stop hiding what hurts, and I lift it up before You — let the power of Christ rest upon me!
Over my body, my mind, my finances and my family, the tent of Your power is pitched today!
No messenger of Satan can buffet me out from under Your covering!
When I am faint, You give me power; when I have no might, You increase my strength!
I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me!
When I am weak, then am I strong!
Save this. Speak it over your house today. The thorn may be in my side, but His power is over my head — His grace is sufficient for me! In Jesus' mighty name, amen!

dreamFire.title: Arise and Go Forward
dreamFire.intro: Tonight's shield prayer is not a guess at your dream — it is heaven's fire sent against every assignment built to hold you in reverse: old altars calling your name, old cycles dressed up as new dreams, and any power still trying to make you relive what God has already closed. Pray it out loud before you sleep and let every attempt to turn you backward be answered by fire tonight.
points: Father, Your Word declares in Deuteronomy 1:6-7, "Ye have dwelt long enough in this mount: Turn you, and take your journey..." Every dream that parks me back at an old mountain, an old season, or a place I already left is cancelled now — I arise, I turn, and I take my journey forward, in the mighty name of Jesus!

Lord, Isaiah 43:18-19 commands me, "Remember ye not the former things... Behold, I will do a new thing..." Every power assigned to drag me back through old dreams, old defeats, and old chapters to make me relive them is silenced tonight — I will not remember what You have told me to forget, in Jesus' mighty name!

Father, by the pattern of Philippians 3:13-14, "forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before, I press toward the mark..." every dream built to pull my eyes backward is overruled — I forget what is behind and I press forward untouched, in the name of Jesus!

I decree tonight according to Numbers 23:23, "Surely there is no enchantment against Jacob, neither is there any divination against Israel..." Every altar lit, every incense raised, every enchantment spoken over my name while I sleep finds no landing ground — there is no enchantment that can stand against this child of God, in the mighty name of Jesus!

Arise, O God, by the authority of Psalm 68:1, "Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered: let them also that hate him flee before him" — every witchcraft table convened to vote for my stagnation, every coven assembled to hold my file open, scatters now and flees before the fire of God, in Jesus' mighty name!

Every power assigned to chase me, trap me, or exchange my forward portion for a backward one in the dream realm tonight, hear the word of Psalm 35:5-6: "Let them be as chaff before the wind: and let the angel of the LORD chase them. Let their way be dark and slippery..." You are now the hunted, your way is dark and slippery before you, and I walk free, in the mighty name of Jesus!

Father, Isaiah 61:3 promises me "the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness" — every garment of stagnation, every mark of sorrow, every covering of delay placed on me in a dream is stripped off and burned, and I receive the garment of praise and forward movement in its place, in the name of Jesus!

By the word of Isaiah 10:27, "his burden shall be taken away from off thy shoulder, and his yoke from off thy neck, and the yoke shall be destroyed because of the anointing" — every yoke of backwardness fastened on me in the dark is destroyed by the anointing upon my life, and I rise up carrying nothing but freedom, in Jesus' mighty name!

Father, Habakkuk 2:3 declares, "though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry" — every dream sent to convince me my vision has failed or my season will never come is a lie exposed tonight; what You have promised is already on its way and cannot be delayed, in the mighty name of Jesus!

I decree by Micah 7:8, "when I fall, I shall arise; when I sit in darkness, the LORD shall be a light unto me" — every dream of falling, sinking, or sitting still in darkness is reversed; I arise, and where I sat in darkness, the light of the Lord now shines, in Jesus' mighty name!

According to Proverbs 4:18, "the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day" — every power assigned to dim my path, confuse my direction, or turn my road back on itself in the dream realm is defeated; my path shines brighter from tonight, in the mighty name of Jesus!

Lord, Revelation 3:8 declares over me, "I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it" — every door shut against me in a dream, every gate locked to hold me back, every entrance barred by a hand in the dark has no power to stand; what You have opened, no destroyer can close, in Jesus' mighty name!

Father, by 2 Corinthians 5:17, "old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new" — every old cycle, old pattern, and old assignment trying to resurrect itself through a dream tonight has no claim on me; I am a new creature, and the old has no right to call me back, in the mighty name of Jesus!

So I decree over tonight, standing on Psalm 121:7-8, "The LORD shall preserve thee from all evil... The LORD shall preserve thy going out and thy coming in from this time forth, and even for evermore" — no backwardness, no altar, no chase, no mark, and no stagnation will touch me between now and sunrise. I will wake moving forward, not backward, in the mighty, all-consuming name of Jesus Christ, amen! 🔥
